idiom_name: page-as-script: request handling, model access and markup emission in one executed view file
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: the view artifact is executed per request and is itself the handler - it reads request parameters, calls the model (repository, DAO or service locator), iterates and branches, and writes markup to the response in the same pass. Two rules keep it survivable: every value that crosses into the output goes through one escaping function, never through raw concatenation, and all model access is funneled through a single call per page so the fetch has one home to change. Where the runtime provides no engine (plain static libraries and low-level languages), the emitter must also own buffering, content type and error handling before the first byte is written. The classic form is justified only for small, short-lived pages; once a second page needs the same data, the fetch belongs in a handler and the view in a template.

pitfalls: Skipping the escaping call at even one interpolation point turns the page into an injection vector.
Calling the model from the render pass hides I/O inside presentation code: no request-level caching, no transaction boundary, no mocking in tests.
The page starts writing before it knows the request is valid; failures then produce truncated responses instead of clean error pages.
Copying the page to make the next one (page-as-template-by-duplication) is the step that makes the approach unmaintainable.

Wrong move: performing the INSERT or UPDATE from the page script on GET -> browsers, crawlers, link prefetchers and caches re-issue GETs with no user intent, so the action duplicates or runs for the wrong visitor -> instead let GET only read state and perform writes in a POST handler behind a CSRF check, per the HTTP safe-method rule the page inherits.

Wrong move: relying on every page to include a shared auth-check snippet -> the next page ships without the include and fails open, so data authorization depends on each author remembering one line -> instead enforce authentication at the container, filter or middleware boundary so no page script is reachable before it has run.

Wrong move: passing data between page sections and included partials through session or request-scope globals -> render order becomes an undocumented dependency, a partial breaks on any page that did not set the variable, and nothing can be exercised in isolation -> instead pass values as explicit locals or parameters into each include and keep the session for genuine cross-request identity.
